page: OVHcloud r3-128 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 2.3 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, this configuration features 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The hardware profile also includes 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps, along with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong memory performance, achieving a top-tier Passmark memory score in the top 10% and strong uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidths of 223.45 GB/sec and 117.55 GB/sec respectively. Single-core CPU performance is also strong, ranking in the top 25% via stress-ng, while multi-core CPU performance and database operations remain in the average tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and text generation for small LLM models also register strong results, though standard Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput align with average mid-tier expectations.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the r3-128 is defined by its dedicated, non-hyperthreaded core allocation, which eliminates resource contention at the CPU level. However, the lack of hyperthreading and AVX-512 support represents a tradeoff for highly parallelized vector-heavy compute tasks. Given its high memory density and strong memory bandwidth, this server is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory databases, caching layers, data processing pipelines, and medium-scale database operations.
